# ledger_bank_institutions (Data Source)

Lists the banks a provider application offers in a country. Ledger asks the provider each time, so the read needs the provider to be reachable: a provider outage or rate limit (`bank_unavailable`, `bank_rate_limited`) fails the read with that code, and it can be retried later. Read only, and needs an API token with the `connections:read` grant. The values are bank-sourced facts as Ledger reports them: they are never edited here, and they are kept apart from your own corrections. Reading changes nothing at the bank, and no consent is started, completed or refreshed (connecting a bank needs you at the bank's own page, in Ledger's UI). Account numbers, balances, provider session references and credentials are never read into Terraform state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The banks an application offers in a country. Ledger asks the provider, so this needs the provider to be reachable.
data "ledger_bank_applications" "all" {}

data "ledger_bank_institutions" "lithuania" {
  application = data.ledger_bank_applications.all.items[0].name
  country     = "LT"
}

output "bank_names" {
  value = [for i in data.ledger_bank_institutions.lithuania.items : i.name]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `application` (String) The name of the application, as `ledger_bank_applications` lists it.
- `country` (String) ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code in capitals, for example `LT`.

### Read-Only

- `items` (Attributes List) The institutions. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items))

<a id="nestedatt--items"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items`

Read-Only:

- `country` (String) The country code.
- `id` (String) The provider's identifier of the bank.
- `max_consent_validity_days` (Number) The longest consent validity in days the bank allows, or 0 when not known.
- `name` (String) The bank's name.
